title: Client Connector on non-persistent Citrix VDIs: the single-user model, the VDI install parameters and the master VM

prose.text: {{single-user-only}} The multi-session product is a separate one: [[cloud-connector.vdi.install]].

prose.label: Advice for non-persistent Citrix VDIs.
prose.text: {{best-practices}} The two install-option rules are also in [[zcc.install.strict-enforcement:citrix-hide-ui]] and [[zcc.install.enrollment:user-domain]].

prose.label: Where the configuration lives.
prose.text: {{vdi-flag}} What else the flag changes is open {{gap:vdi-flag-scope}}. {{config-timeout}} The parameter's unit and default are in [[zcc.install.windows-unattended:config-timeout]].

prose.label: The filter driver.
prose.text: {{install-lwf}} {{lwf-boot-start}} The driver switches themselves are in [[zcc.install.windows-driver]].

prose.label: Open points.
prose.text: How the revert option, which is not supported for non-persistent VDI ([[zcc.install.revert:scope]]), interacts with these parameters is open {{gap:revert-interaction}}.

single-user-only.statement: Client Connector supports only a dedicated, single-user VDI model; for multi-session VDIs, Client Connector for VDI is required. The MSI and EXE install-options pages both say so.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector only supports a dedicated, single-user virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) model. For multi-session VDIs, Zscaler Client Connector for VDI is required.
Zscaler Client Connector only supports a dedicated, single-user virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) model. For multi-session VDIs, Zscaler Client Connector for VDI is required.

best-practices.statement: For non-persistent Citrix VDIs, Zscaler recommends not logging in to Client Connector on the master VM; the strict enforcement install option requires the hide-app-UI-on-launch option disabled so the app can remind users to enroll before they reach the internet; and the user domain option requires Integrated Windows Authentication (IWA). The MSI and EXE pages say the same with their own option names.

quotes: Deploying Zscaler Client Connector with Non-Persistent Citrix VDIs
Zscaler recommends that you don't log in to Zscaler Client Connector on the master VM.
To use the STRICTENFORCEMENT install option, you must have the HIDEAPPUIONLAUNCH install option disabled.
This allows Zscaler Client Connector to remind users to enroll with Zscaler Client Connector before accessing the internet.
To use the USERDOMAIN install option, you must use Integrated Windows Authentication (IWA).
Deploying Zscaler Client Connector with Non-Persistent Citrix VDIs
Zscaler recommends that you don't log in to Zscaler Client Connector on the master VM.
To use the --strictEnforcement install option, you must have the --hideAppUIOnLaunch install option disabled.
This allows Zscaler Client Connector to remind users to enroll with Zscaler Client Connector before accessing the internet.
To use the --userDomain install option, you must use Integrated Windows Authentication (IWA).

vdi-flag.statement: VDI=1 (EXE --vdi 1) makes Client Connector store its configuration data in the %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\Zscaler user profile store instead of the default %ProgramData%\Zscaler, so a profile management tool such as Citrix UPM can roam and restore it.

quotes: VDI=1 : Configures the Zscaler Client Connector to store configuration data in the %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\Zscaler user profile store so it is roamed using a profile management tool instead of the default %ProgramData%\Zscaler.
This allows admins to restore Zscaler's configuration as part of users' profiles using tools such as Citrix UPM
--vdi 1 : Configures the Zscaler Client Connector to store configuration data in the %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\Zscaler user profile store

config-timeout.statement: In environments with roaming profiles such as non-persistent VDIs, CONFIGTIMEOUT=300 makes the app wait the specified interval for its configuration data to be restored when it is not found, because a profile management solution might need extra time to restore it. If the VDI deployment does not use a profile management solution, the MSI and EXE pages say the parameter is not necessary.

quotes: CONFIGTIMEOUT=300 : If the Zscaler Client Connector configuration data is not found, Zscaler Client Connector waits for the specified interval for configuration data to be restored.

In environments with roaming profiles such as non-persistent VDIs, it might take additional time for the profile management solution to restore the Zscaler Client Connector configuration data to the user profile.
If the VDI deployment does not use a profile management solution, it's not necessary to apply the CONFIGTIMEOUT parameter.
If the VDI deployment does not use a profile management solution, it's not necessary to apply the --configTimeout parameter.

install-lwf.statement: INSTALLLWFDRIVER=1 (EXE --installLWFDriver 1) installs the lightweight filter driver used for traffic interception during installation. Without it, the MSI page says Client Connector does not install the driver until a forwarding profile configures it during policy download, which might cause network connection disruption and VDI disconnection.

quotes: INSTALLLWFDRIVER=1 : Install the lightweight filter driver used for traffic interception during installation of the Zscaler Client Connector.

Without this parameter, Zscaler Client Connector doesn't install the LWF driver until configured to do so by a forwarding profile during policy download, which might cause network connection disruption and VDI disconnection.
--installLWFDriver 1 : Install the lightweight filter (LWF) driver used for traffic interception during installation of the Zscaler Client Connector.

lwf-boot-start.statement: LWFBOOTSTART=1 configures the LWF driver to load at system boot instead of the default at system startup, which the MSI page says prevents a blue screen during OS boot where the OS is booted over the network, such as in Citrix Provisioning Services. With Citrix Provisioning Server the option is required (--LWFBootStart in the EXE).

quotes: LWFBOOTSTART=1 : Configures the LWF driver to load at system boot instead of the default at system startup.
This prevents a blue screen during OS boot in environments where the OS is booted over the network, such as in Citrix Provisioning Services.
If you are using Citrix Provisioning Server, you must use the LWFBOOTSTART option.
If you are using Citrix Provisioning Server, you must use the --LWFBootStart option.

master-vm.statement: On the master VM, Citrix UPM is configured to back up and restore {UserProfileFolder}\AppData\Roaming\Zscaler, and the installer runs with the sample parameters msiexec/i ZCC_installer.msi USERDOMAIN=<AD domain> CLOUDNAME=<cloudname> VDI=1 CONFIGTIMEOUT=300 INSTALLLWFDRIVER=1 LWFBOOTSTART=1, or --vdi 1 --configTimeout 300 --installLWFDriver 1 --LWFBootStart 1 for the EXE; the MSI page calls the parameters samples.

quotes: Configure Citrix UPM to backup and restore to the following folder: {UserProfileFolder}\AppData\Roaming\Zscaler
msiexec/i ZCC_installer.msi USERDOMAIN=<AD domain> CLOUDNAME=<cloudname> VDI=1 CONFIGTIMEOUT=300 INSTALLLWFDRIVER=1 LWFBOOTSTART=1
The parameters listed earlier are samples for a VDI installation Zscaler Client Connector.
--vdi 1 --configTimeout 300 --installLWFDriver 1 --LWFBootStart 1

vdi-flag-scope.title: Whether VDI=1 changes anything beyond the configuration store
vdi-flag-scope.detail: The install-options pages say VDI=1 moves the configuration store to the user profile (claim vdi-flag). They do not say whether the flag changes any other Client Connector behavior.
vdi-flag-scope.blocks: deciding whether a virtual desktop install needs the flag for any reason other than roaming the configuration

revert-interaction.title: How the unsupported revert option interacts with the VDI parameters
revert-interaction.detail: The revert page says the revert option is not supported for non-persistent VDI. The install-options pages for VDI do not mention revert, and neither page says what happens if a revert is attempted on a VDI installed with these parameters.
